video_metadata.title: 200 SMA Bounce Strategy on MES — How I Use the 200 MA as a Floor and Ceiling

input.transcript_snippet: Today I want to show you the 200 SMA bounce strategy I've been trading on the MES for the last two years. The idea is simple — the 200-period simple moving average on the 15-minute chart acts as a massive support and resistance level. Institutional players watch this level closely. When price comes down and tests the 200 SMA from above, and we get a rejection — I like to see a pin bar or a wick — I go long. When price is below the 200 SMA and rallies up to test it from underneath, and we see it acting as ceiling, I go short. It's a bidirectional setup. I don't care whether the market is going up or down overall — if we're near that 200 SMA and we get a rejection candle I'm looking to trade it. I only do this during regular trading hours, not overnight. I use ATR for my stop, about one and a half times ATR below the swing low on a long. I target back toward VWAP or the previous high/low depending on where we are. I also check the daily trend first — I want the 4H to be somewhat aligned but it's not a hard rule. I check the economic calendar too, I don't trade around FOMC or CPI. Win rate on this for me is around 65 percent, profit factor about 2.1.

strategies.description: Bidirectional 200 SMA bounce on MES 15m — price tests the 200 SMA and prints a rejection candle; long when SMA is support, short when SMA is resistance; RTH only, skip FOMC/CPI per FuturesEdge Pro YouTube walkthrough.
strategies.entry_condition: Price tests the 200-period SMA from above (support) and prints a pin bar or wick rejection; enter long on the confirmation bar close. SHORT: price tests the 200-period SMA from below (resistance) and prints a rejection candle; enter short. Both sides require RTH session and no FOMC/CPI on calendar. HTF (4H) alignment preferred but not required.
strategies.bias_condition: 4H chart provides HTF directional context for bounce direction preference
